"""Mid-word syllable fragments, layers.0.mlp.down_proj:3457.

The component is negative on pieces of longer words that are split across tokens and
carry an 'n' in the middle of a syllable: a piece with no leading space, made of letters,
containing a vowel-n-vowel run ('iner', 'inal', 'ener', 'anic', 'onom', 'ination'). Its
strongest responses are to the -ner / -nom pieces ('ner', 'nen', 'onomic', 'conom'),
which get a further push down. Every other token is predicted as 0.
"""
import re

READS = ()

VOWEL_N_VOWEL = re.compile(r"[aeiouy]n[aeiouy]")
NER_NOM = re.compile(r"ner|nom")
BASE = -0.10       # per-token response to a mid-word vowel-n-vowel piece
NER_EXTRA = -0.23  # added for pieces that also contain 'ner' or 'nom'


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    piece = token.strip()
    is_mid_word = piece.isalpha() and not token.startswith(" ")
    value = 0.0
    if is_mid_word and VOWEL_N_VOWEL.search(piece.lower()):
        value = BASE
        if NER_NOM.search(piece.lower()):
            value += NER_EXTRA
    return carry, value

"""Give an n-bearing letter piece a negative estimate when it follows
a letter in the same document."""
READS = ()
N_LIKE = frozenset('nн')

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].casefold()
    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ''
    same_document = (len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and
                     prefix.document_ids[-1] == prefix.document_ids[-2])
    continues_word = (same_document and bool(previous) and bool(token) and
                      previous[-1].isalpha() and token[0].isalpha())
    has_n = any(letter in token for letter in N_LIKE)
    return None, -0.03 if continues_word and has_n else 0.0

"""Respond to English quantifiers, especially each/all/both, and to only.

The previous word adjusts the response for local grammatical context.
Conditions, negation, possession and action verbs increase it; grammatical
subjects, copulas, articles and punctuation decrease it. Capitalization and
unspaced code/name tokens weaken the response. It also recognizes several
French, Spanish, Russian and Chinese quantifiers, and -ing words immediately
after "without". Document boundaries reset context; other words receive zero.
"""
READS = ()

BASE = {'each': 1.07, 'all': 0.55, 'both': 0.43, 'only': 0.31,
        'every': 0.16, 'any': 0.01, 'no': 0.05,
        'neither': 0.31, 'none': 0.30, 'solely': 0.30}
CAPITAL = {'each': 0.74, 'all': 0.14, 'both': 0.14, 'only': 0.13,
           'every': -0.19, 'any': -0.20, 'no': -0.06,
           'neither': 0.10, 'none': 0.12, 'solely': 0.10}
CONTEXT = {'for': -0.18, 'in': -0.14, 'at': -0.21, 'to': -0.08,
           'of': -0.07, 'with': 0.29, 'over': 0.26, 'through': 0.19,
           'after': 0.20, 'where': 0.43, 'that': 0.07, 'if': 0.24,
           'when': 0.26, 'which': 0.19, 'not': 0.36, 'without': 0.79}
LIGHT_WORDS = set('''is are am was were be been being
    i you he she it we they us them him her
    can could will would shall should may might must do does did
    a an the this these those my your our their his its and or but nor'''.split())
ACTIONS = set('''use find get select remove replace include contain add
    multiply divide write compute calculate assign check need require keep
    cover reach affect depend'''.split())


def is_action(word):
    if word in ACTIONS or word in {'found', 'written', 'kept'}:
        return True
    for ending in ('s', 'es', 'ed', 'ing'):
        if word.endswith(ending):
            stem = word[:-len(ending)]
            if stem in ACTIONS or stem + 'e' in ACTIONS:
                return True
    return word.endswith('ies') and word[:-3] + 'y' in ACTIONS


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = raw.strip().strip('._')
    lower = word.lower()
    # Familiar translations of 'each', 'all', and 'only'.
    if lower in {'cada', 'chaque', '各', '每个', '的所有'}:
        return None, 0.45
    if lower in {'每', '每一', '所有', 'все', 'всех', 'каждый', 'каждой'}:
        return None, 0.30
    if lower in {'全部', 'только'}:
        return None, 0.23
    if lower not in BASE:
        same_doc = (prefix.position > 0 and
                    prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1])
        if (same_doc and word.isalpha() and word.endswith('ing') and
                prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() == 'without'):
            return None, 0.40
        return None, 0.0
    if word != lower:
        if word.isupper() and lower == 'all':
            return None, 0.45
        return None, CAPITAL[lower]
    if not raw.startswith(' '):
        return None, 0.84 if lower == 'each' else 0.45 * BASE[lower]
    value = BASE[lower]
    if (prefix.position == 0 or
            prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]):
        return None, value + 0.34
    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    prev = previous.strip().lower()
    value += CONTEXT.get(prev, 0.0)
    if prev in LIGHT_WORDS:
        value -= 0.10
    elif prev in {'because', 'since', 'unless', 'until'}:
        value += 0.24
    elif prev in {'has', 'have', 'had'}:
        value += 0.18
    elif is_action(prev):
        value += 0.35
    if any(c in previous for c in ',;:'):
        value -= 0.18
    if prev.isdigit():
        value -= 0.10
    if prev.endswith('ing'):
        value += 0.14
    return None, value

programs.sol:
"""Detect compiler/abstract-syntax vocabulary, not arbitrary programming text.

Syntax forms (Expr, Statement, Token, etc.) give large negative values; names,
values, and source metadata give smaller ones.  Identifier capitalization and
member-name punctuation usually strengthen the response relative to prose.
Repeated parser terminology adds a short-lived context boost.  The first token
of a document gets a larger lexical response.  Tool-call, thought, and turn
delimiters have fixed negative values; other vocabulary is left at zero.
"""
import re
from functools import cache

READS = ()

# Responses by spelling: spaced lowercase, spaced capitalized, unspaced
# lowercase/all-caps, unspaced capitalized, and member/argument punctuation.
# The groups are ordered from specific syntax concepts to general code words.
GROUPS = (
    # Syntax abbreviations.
    (
        'expr stmt decl',
        (-1.87, -2.65, -2.2, -3.57, -3.17),
    ),
    # Syntax forms.
    (
        'expression expressions statement statements declaration '
        'declarations declarator',
        (-0.37, -0.78, -1.04, -2.76, -1.83),
    ),
    # Lexical syntax.
    (
        'lexer lexeme token tokens ast syntax sexp identifier identifiers '
        'literal literals callee clause',
        (-1.1, -1.47, -0.73, -1.77, -1.7),
    ),
    # Compiler operations.
    (
        'parse parsed parser parsing eval interpreter isinstance instanceof '
        'compiler codegen visitor',
        (-0.84, -1.1, -1.07, -1.06, -0.98),
    ),
    # Typed entities and operations.
    (
        'type types kind variable variables var vars function functions func '
        'fn method methods call constructor closure assign binary unary',
        (-0.14, -0.41, -0.32, -0.96, -0.85),
    ),
    # Object and definition syntax.
    (
        'class object property field element block document module member '
        'tag leaf def const constant import',
        (-0.04, -0.17, -0.08, -0.57, -0.56),
    ),
    # Object metadata.
    (
        'name names value values val node nodes rule rules pattern signature '
        'attr attrs attribute attributes annotation arguments argument args '
        'arg kwargs',
        (-0.31, -0.32, -0.54, -0.82, -0.68),
    ),
    # Source description.
    (
        'code program snippet line lines column columns location source key '
        'keys label labels',
        (-0.13, -0.18, -0.23, -0.45, -0.48),
    ),
    # Scope.
    (
        'scope binding symbol symbols namespace resolver resolve',
        (-0.25, -0.54, -0.39, -0.99, -1.03),
    ),
    # Source-language tooling and notation.
    (
        'ident metavar operand opcode instruction specifier paren '
        'parentheses indent indentation inline lint eslint cli execute exec '
        'pp',
        (-0.42, -0.49, -0.41, -1.3, -0.93),
    ),
)
WORD_GROUP = {word: i for i, (words, _) in enumerate(GROUPS)
              for word in words.split()}
PARSER_TERMS = set("""
expr stmt decl lexer lexeme parser ast syntax token identifier
literal codegen
""".split())

@cache
def lexical(s):
    """Current token's lexical response and whether it mentions parser syntax."""
    clean = s.strip()
    body = clean.lstrip('._-/([<{\\')
    if not body or not body.isascii() or not body.isalpha():
        return 0.0, False
    # Separate acronym boundaries as well as ordinary camel-case boundaries.
    words = re.sub(r'([A-Z])([A-Z][a-z])', r'\1 \2', body)
    pieces = re.sub(r'([a-z])([A-Z])', r'\1 \2', words).lower().split()
    # PP without identifier punctuation is often an unrelated word fragment.
    if body.lower() == 'pp' and not clean.startswith('_'):
        return 0.0, False
    groups = [WORD_GROUP[w] for w in pieces if w in WORD_GROUP]
    if not groups:
        return 0.0, False
    cue = any(w in PARSER_TERMS for w in pieces)
    member = clean.startswith(('.', '_', '(', '[', '<'))
    if body.lower() in ('nodetype', 'objecttype'):
        return (-3.2 if member else -2.0), cue
    if member:
        style = 4
    elif s[:1].isspace():
        style = 1 if body[0].isupper() else 0
    else:
        style = 3 if body[0].isupper() and not body.isupper() else 2
    value = GROUPS[min(groups)][1][style]
    # Compounds naming two code concepts, such as propertyName or KeyCode.
    if len(groups) > 1:
        value -= 0.6
    return value, cue


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        recent, first = 0.0, True
    else:
        recent, first = carry[1], False
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value, cue = lexical(s)
    if value:
        value = value * (1.75 if first else 1.0) - 0.35 * recent
    if s == '<tool_call>':
        value = -1.35
    elif s == '<|im_end|>':
        value = -0.10
    elif s in ('<think>', '</think>'):
        value = -0.20
    recent = min(3.0, 0.9 * recent + float(cue))
    return (doc, recent), float(value)
programs.haiku:
"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:3459 -- a "programming vocabulary" detector.

This component writes into the residual stream mostly as a *negative* signal on
words that name pieces of code: compiler/parser internals (Expr, Literal, Token,
Parser, Visitor, AST, rule, node, pattern), and more loosely calls, types, names,
arguments and values (Type, name, arguments, key, value, var, function, code).
It is also strongly negative on the tool-call marker <tool_call>. Elsewhere, in
ordinary prose and punctuation, it is near zero.

The program looks only at the newest token. It splits the token into words at
camelCase and underscore boundaries (FunctionType -> function, type; _expr -> expr),
then predicts a strong negative value for a parser/compiler word, a medium negative
value for a general code word, and 0 otherwise. The values are scaled to the
component's typical size (about -0.8 and -0.4 nats of activation).
"""

import re

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Words naming parser / compiler / syntax-tree concepts: strongest.
PARSER = {"literal", "visitor", "parser", "parse", "parsed", "expression", "expr",
          "interpreter", "resolver", "resolve", "resolved", "token", "syntax", "ast",
          "grammar", "macro", "node", "pattern", "rule", "rules", "tree", "lexer",
          "clause", "codegen", "attribute", "lint", "eslint", "typescript"}
# Words naming calls, types, names and values in code: medium.
CODE = {"call", "invoke", "invocation", "func", "function", "args", "arg", "arguments",
        "argument", "kwargs", "type", "typeof", "env", "stack", "exec", "execute",
        "execution", "instruction", "instructions", "dispatch", "var", "variable",
        "variables", "snippet", "kind", "name", "names", "key", "value", "values",
        "code", "schema", "tool", "cli"}


def words(token: str) -> list[str]:
    """Lower-case words of a token, split at camelCase and non-letter boundaries."""
    token = re.sub(r"([a-z0-9])([A-Z])", r"\1 \2", token)
    return [w.lower() for w in re.findall(r"[A-Za-z]+", token)]


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token.strip() == "<tool_call>":
        return None, -1.0
    found = words(token)
    if any(w in PARSER for w in found):
        return None, -0.8
    if any(w in CODE for w in found):
        return None, -0.4
    return None, 0.0

"""Component layers.0.mlp.down_proj:3460, the "in" detector.

This component writes a strong signal into the residual stream on the word "in",
the preposition, in whatever spelling the tokenizer gave it:

- " in" (space + lowercase, the usual preposition): about 1.45
- " In", "In" (capitalised, e.g. at the start of a sentence): about 1.85
- other punctuation or space prefixed forms such as "-in", "/in", "_in", "(in", " IN": about 1.45
- a bare lowercase "in" with no leading space, usually a piece of a longer word: about 0.5
- bare "IN" (uppercase, no space): about 0.25

Every other token gives 0. It fires at the position of the "in" token itself, and it
does not depend on the previous tokens in any way this program models.

The program needs no state: each position is judged from its own token string alone.
"""

READS = ()


def core(tok):
    """The token with its leading punctuation, spaces and quotes removed."""
    i = 0
    while i < len(tok) and not tok[i].isalpha():
        i += 1
    return tok[i:]


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = core(tok)
    if word.lower() != "in":
        return None, 0.0
    if tok == "in":
        return None, 0.5
    if tok == "IN":
        return None, 0.25
    if word == "In":
        return None, 1.85
    return None, 1.45

programs.sol:
"""Directional particle word-pieces, strongest for 'out', then 'up'/'down'.

Predict a negative response to a small directional vocabulary. Weaken it in
listed conventional verb-particle constructions, such as 'turn out', 'set up'
and 'break down'; some selecting heads reverse the sign of 'on'. Case
and attachment to another word or identifier matter.
A few Chinese/Japanese out/off equivalents also get negative responses.
Everything else is zero; small unrelated lexical effects are not modeled.
The only memory is the preceding trailing word, reset at document boundaries.
"""
import re

READS = ()
# Space-prefixed lowercase word-pieces: negative strengths.
PARTICLES = {
    'out': 5.2,
    'up': 2.6,
    'down': 2.4,
    'off': 1.7,
    'back': 1.5,
    'over': 1.13,
    'away': 1.4,
    'along': 1.2,
    'across': 1.13,
    'through': 0.85,
    'together': 0.86,
    'around': 0.56,
    'apart': 0.48,
    'on': 0.49,
}
# Common selecting heads for particles/prepositions, grouped by strength.
PHRASAL = {
    'out': (
        (0.9, 'turn stand'),
        (2.0, 'carry check find figure point set'),
        (3.2, 'come cut take work run break fall pull bring put stick roll '
              'lay drop hang throw wipe fill pour'),
        (3.8, 'filter print pick rule'),
    ),
    'up': (
        (0.55, 'set'),
        (0.95, 'end come pick show open add turn pop break wrap clear'),
        (1.2, 'build'),
        (1.4, 'take put bring wake grow clean blow mess follow look hold '
              'stand hang wind throw'),
        (1.75, 'give sign catch make match sum round roll lock'),
        (2.2, 'keep pull go'),
    ),
    'down': (
        (0.35, 'shut break'),
        (0.9, 'sit pull lay slide drop boil'),
        (1.2, 'come take put cut set fall knock bring turn close hold roll'),
        (1.6, 'slow look lie step scroll narrow write'),
    ),
    'on': (
        (-0.16, 'base rely'),
        (-0.3, 'depend dependence dependency'),
        (0.0, 'focus work hold'),
        (0.15, 'act play take impact effect'),
    ),
}
IRREGULAR = {
    'built': 'build', 'caught': 'catch', 'stood': 'stand',
    'slid': 'slide', 'hung': 'hang', 'threw': 'throw', 'thrown': 'throw',
    'lying': 'lie', 'went': 'go', 'grown': 'grow', 'found': 'find',
    'came': 'come', 'taken': 'take', 'took': 'take',
    'ran': 'run', 'sat': 'sit', 'laid': 'lay', 'grew': 'grow',
    'brought': 'bring', 'woke': 'wake', 'woken': 'wake',
    'gave': 'give', 'given': 'give', 'made': 'make',
    'broken': 'break', 'broke': 'break', 'fallen': 'fall', 'fell': 'fall',
    'blew': 'blow', 'blown': 'blow', 'dependent': 'depend',
}


def inflections(root):
    forms = {root, root + 's', root + 'es', root + 'ed', root + 'ing'}
    if root.endswith('e'):
        forms.update((root + 'd', root[:-1] + 'ing'))
    if root.endswith('y'):
        forms.update((root[:-1] + 'ies', root[:-1] + 'ied'))
    if root in {'set', 'sit', 'run', 'put', 'cut', 'drop', 'wrap',
                'sum', 'pop', 'step'}:
        forms.update((root + root[-1] + 'ed', root + root[-1] + 'ing'))
    return forms


# Expand English inflections, rather than listing token IDs or corpus bigrams.
PHRASE_FORMS = {
    particle: {form: strength
               for strength, roots in groups
               for root in roots.split()
               for form in inflections(root)}
    for particle, groups in PHRASAL.items()
}


# A bare word-piece is often attached inside an identifier or longer word.
BARE = {'out': 3.1, 'up': 0.75, 'down': 1.2, 'on': 0.05,
        'off': 1.05, 'over': 0.7, 'back': 0.95, 'around': 0.2}
COMPOUND = {'out': 4.5, 'up': 1.45, 'down': 2.05, 'off': 1.0}
DERIVATIVES = {'outside': 0.94, 'outer': 1.0, 'outward': 1.35,
               'throughout': 0.8, 'outs': 2.0, 'ups': 0.6, 'downs': 2.2}
OUT_EQUIVALENTS = {'出': 0.4, '出来': 0.4, '出來': 0.4,
                   '出去': 1.0, '掉': 0.4, 'アウト': 2.8}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    original = token.strip().lstrip('-_/.')
    word = original.lower()
    strength = PARTICLES.get(word, DERIVATIVES.get(word, 0.0))
    if strength:
        if original.istitle():
            strength = {'out': 6.0, 'up': 2.5, 'down': 3.0,
                        'off': 2.3, 'on': 1.0}.get(word, strength * 1.1)
            if not token[0].isspace() and word in {'out', 'up', 'down'}:
                strength *= 0.8
        elif original.isupper():
            strength = {'out': 5.0, 'up': 1.1, 'on': 0.58}.get(word, strength)
            if not token[0].isspace():
                strength *= 0.75
        elif token[0].isspace():
            verb = IRREGULAR.get(previous, previous)
            strength = PHRASE_FORMS.get(word, {}).get(verb, strength)
            if previous == 'way' and word in {'out', 'up', 'down'}:
                strength *= 1.4
        elif token.startswith(('-', '_', '/')):
            strength = COMPOUND.get(word, strength)
        elif token.startswith('.'):
            strength = {'out': 1.5, 'on': 0.9, 'down': 3.0}.get(word, strength)
        else:
            strength = BARE.get(word, strength)
            if word == 'on' and not previous:
                strength = 0.7
            elif not previous and word in {'out', 'up', 'down'}:
                strength = {'out': 4.8, 'up': 2.7, 'down': 2.6}[word]
    elif re.fullmatch(r'on[A-Z][a-zA-Z]*', original):
        strength = 0.6  # Event-handler names, e.g. onClick.
    else:
        strength = OUT_EQUIVALENTS.get(word, 0.0)
    joined = previous + token.lower()
    match = re.search(r'[a-z]+$', joined)
    following = match.group()[-32:] if match else ''
    return (doc, following), float(-strength)

"""Directional particles (layers.0.mlp.down_proj:3461), with a context damper.

This component reads English adverb particles that finish a phrasal verb or a
direction phrase, such as "speak OUT", "stepped UP", "shut DOWN", "switched OFF",
"came BACK", "ran AWAY", "over", "along", "through". It goes negative on them, and
it is near zero on nearly every other token.

How strong it is depends on the particle:
  out                  strongest (about -4)
  down, up, off, back, away   medium (about -1.7)
  over, along, across, through, together, outside, around   weaker (about -1)
  on                   weakest (about -0.4)

It is weaker (about 40% as strong) when "out" follows a light verb or a
code/identifier word: "turned out", "set up", "check out", "find out", "carried out",
"System.out". Those are idioms in which the particle is less of a direction.

The program looks at the current token, and the one before it inside the same
document. It ignores case and a leading space.
"""

READS = ()

STRENGTH = {
    "out": -4.0,

"""Detect typographic rules: repeated punctuation used for separators or blanks.

subword token. Medium-width rules can be stronger than very long ones. A line

token. Comment delimiters around a rule are allowed.

RULE_STRENGTH = {
    '-': (0.02, 0.18, 0.50, 1.02, 1.20, 0.90, 0.93),
    '=': (0.11, 0.20, 0.86, 1.55, 1.36, 1.31, 1.26),
    '_': (0.08, 0.14, 0.47, 0.75, 1.04, 0.75, 0.75),
    '.': (-0.02, 0.01, 0.38, 0.62, 0.94, 0.81, 0.81),
    '*': (0.07, 0.18, 0.88, 1.28, 1.42, 1.16, 0.94),
    '#': (0.00, 0.00, 0.70, 1.28, 1.44, 1.07, 0.95),
    '~': (0.00, 0.22, 0.60, 1.01, 1.25, 1.00, 0.90),
    '/': (0.00, 0.00, 0.40, 1.03, 1.03, 1.00, 0.85),
    '!': (-0.06, 0.04, 0.51, 0.60, 0.70, 0.80, 0.80),
}

    '<think>': 0.076,
    '</think>': 0.209,
    '<tool_response>': 0.143,
    '<tool_call>': -0.113,
    '<|im_end|>': 0.034,
}
RUN = re.compile(r'([\-=_.\*#~/!])\1{2,}')


def strength(mark, width):
    values = RULE_STRENGTH[mark]
    for i in range(1, len(WIDTHS)):
        if width <= WIDTHS[i]:
            fraction = (width - WIDTHS[i - 1]) / (WIDTHS[i] - WIDTHS[i - 1])
            return values[i - 1] + fraction * (values[i] - values[i - 1])
    return values[-1]

    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = int(prefix.document_ids[-1])

    if run is None:
        return carry, 0.0
    # Only whitespace and comment openers/closers may surround a rule.
    outside = text[:run.start()] + text[run.end():]

Fires on a token that is a long run of one punctuation mark, the kind a document
uses to draw a rule or underline a heading: '================', '----------------',
'________________', '................'. Such a token has no word in it, just the one
symbol repeated. The response grows with the run's length, reaching full strength at
16 characters, and depends on the symbol: '=', '*', '#', '-', '~', '+', '^' are
strongest, '_' and '.' weaker. Two chat-markup tokens also carry a small response.
Everything else is predicted as 0."""

SYMBOL_STRENGTH = {"=": 1.4, "*": 1.4, "#": 1.2, "-": 1.2, "~": 1.2, "+": 1.2, "^": 1.2, "/": 1.0,
                   "_": 0.8, ".": 0.8}
MARKUP_STRENGTH = {"</think>": 0.2, "<tool_response>": 0.14}
MIN_RUN, FULL_RUN = 5, 16


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token in MARKUP_STRENGTH:

    ramp = min(1.0, (len(text) - MIN_RUN + 1) / (FULL_RUN - MIN_RUN + 1))

    (set('completely entirely fully totally nearly almost largely very quite '

    (set('exactly actually literally truly simply essentially directly'.split()),

"thousand", "hundred", their plurals, the Chinese scale words 千, 万, 亿

"миллион" or "Millionen". It is strongest on "million" and "billion"
(about 6-8), a bit lower on "thousand" and "hundred" (about 3-6). The word
"of" right after "thousands", "millions" or "hundreds" fires too ("thousands
of", about 5.5). Inside a number, a repeated digit also fires: the second 0 of
"00" (as in 1000, 2004) at about 0.7, and the second 9 or 8 of "99" or "98"
at about 0.5-0.75. Everything else predicts 0.

carries no state across positions.

SCALE = {
    "hundred": 3.0, "hundreds": 2.5, "百": 2.2,
    "thousand": 6.5, "thousands": 5.7, "千": 6.6,
    "million": 6.4, "millions": 7.0, "万": 5.5, "萬": 5.6,
    "billion": 7.4, "billions": 8.0, "trillion": 7.9, "亿": 7.9, "億": 7.2,
    "百万": 10.3, "千万": 9.5,
}
# Characters that mark a large-number unit inside a longer token.
BIG_CHARS = "千万亿萬億"
# Plural quantity words that are often followed by "of".
PLURAL_QUANTITY = {"thousands", "millions", "hundreds"}
# (previous digit, this digit) pairs inside a number, e.g. "00", "99", "98".

    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = tok.strip().lower()
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    prev_word = prev.strip().lower()
    if word in SCALE:
        return carry, SCALE[word]
    if word == "of" and prev_word in PLURAL_QUANTITY:
        return carry, 5.5 if prev_word != "hundreds" else 2.5
    if any(c in BIG_CHARS for c in tok) or "illion" in word:

    return carry, REPEAT.get((prev, tok), 0.0)

"""Approximate a mostly negative detector of standalone indentation/padding.

Non-whitespace tokens and isolated single spaces return zero. Horizontal blank
runs get a response calibrated by their width, document position, preceding
line break, and recent/document-wide spacing density. Tabs count as four
columns; width also has a four-column remainder correction. Space-padded
newline tokens use a separate, weaker calibration. State resets per document.
The constants were fitted on training activations, without word/token lookups.
"""
import math
from collections import deque

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, 0, 0, 0, 0, "", "", deque(maxlen=32))
    (doc, position, spaces, tabs, newlines,
     previous, before_previous, recent) = carry
    blank = bool(text) and not text.strip(" \t")
    width = text.count(" ") + 4 * text.count("\t")
    value = 0.0
    n = position + 1
    recent_root = math.sqrt(sum(recent) / (len(recent) + 1))
    if blank and (len(text) > 1 or text == "\t"):
        has_tabs = "\t" in text
        begins_line = ("\n" in previous or previous.endswith("\\n")
                       or (previous == "n" and "\\" in before_previous))
        # Shape of the blank run; tabs count as four columns.
        shape = (-0.538 + 0.338 * math.log1p(width)
                 - 0.403 * (width % 4 == 1) + 0.556 * (width == 2)
                 - 0.354 * has_tabs
                 + 1.160 * (has_tabs and " " not in text))
        # Heavy initial response, fading as the document grows.
        beginning = -(4.039 + 0.387 * min(width, 12)) / n
        # Dense indentation strengthens it; intervening lines dilute it.
        context = (-0.539 * recent_root - 0.361 * spaces / n
                   - 3.622 * tabs / n + 2.498 * newlines / n
                   - 0.540 * begins_line)
        value = shape + beginning + context
    elif ("\n" in text and text.count(" ") >= 2
          and not text.strip(" \t\r\n")):
        # A padded blank line: the whitespace response is much weaker.
        log_width = math.log1p(width)
        value = (-0.105 + 0.277 * log_width
                 - 0.171 * log_width * math.sqrt(spaces / n)
                 - 0.158 * recent_root - 1.615 * tabs / n

"""Indentation detector for layer 0's MLP, output 3484 (writes into the residual stream).

What it does: this component goes negative on indentation: a token made only of
spaces and/or tabs ("    ", "\t\t", "       "). On every other token it is about zero.
The size of the dip depends on a few plain things:
  * line start: indentation right after a line break (previous token ends in "\n")
    dips more than indentation in the middle of a line;
  * indentation density: the share of the document so far that was indentation.
    Code-like text, where indentation is frequent, dips more; prose, where it is
    rare, dips less;
  * width: wider indentation dips a little more;
  * the first token of a document (no context yet) dips the most.

Written in terms of tokens and document position only; no model internals.
"""

import math

READS = ()

BASE = -1.46        # typical level for indentation
LINE_START = -0.44  # extra dip when the indentation begins a line
DENSITY = -0.46     # per unit of log(indentation density)
WIDTH = -0.18       # per unit of log(indentation width in columns)
FIRST = -4.36       # extra dip on the first token of a document


def _is_indent(token):
    # two or more spaces/tabs, or a single tab; a lone space is ordinary text
    return (len(token) >= 2 or token == "\t") and all(c in " \t" for c in token)


def _width(token):
    return sum(4 if c == "\t" else 1 for c in token)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document id, index where this document starts, indentation tokens so far)
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    t = prefix.position
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, t, 0)
    _, start, indents = carry
    n = t - start  # tokens of this document before the current one
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if not _is_indent(token):
        return (doc, start, indents), 0.0
    line_start = t > 0 and "\n" in prefix.token_strings[-2]
    density = (indents + 1) / (n + 1)
    value = BASE + DENSITY * math.log(density) + WIDTH * math.log(_width(token))
    if line_start:
        value += LINE_START
    if n == 0:
        value += FIRST
    return (doc, start, indents + 1), value

token is the syllable "on", or a short token ending in "on": " on", "on", "ON", "ron",

# Letters not listed (most consonants) give about 3.4.
